name: Bitly
whyPeoplePay: Bitly's real product is a promise about the future: links shortened on their domain in 2012 still resolve today. You are renting somebody else's commitment to keep a redirect alive, plus the click analytics, the QR codes and the branded domain handling that a marketing team wants in one place.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: A small monthly allowance of links and QR codes.

plans.name: Core
plans.note: $120 a year on the annual plan, which is how the page presents it.

plans.name: Growth
plans.note: $348 a year on the annual plan, shown as $29/month billed annually.

plans.name: Premium
plans.note: $2,388 a year on the annual plan, shown as $199/month billed annually.

pricing.note: Monthly-billed figures recorded, with the annual-billed equivalents in each plan note, because the page advertises savings of up to 34% on annual billing and quoting only the annual rate would understate what a month-to-month subscriber actually pays.

ranked.rationale: Gives you the two things that matter and takes on the one that is hard. You get your own short domain, real redirects and per-link visit counts through a documented REST API that the third-party apps already speak. What you take on is the promise: the domain registration, the certificate and the database row are now yours to keep alive, and Bitly's entire pitch is that they do that part for you.
